rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation on completed consistent inputs; i2441 (2025) p.5 Line12 takes W-2 box10 less the portion already included in box1. The project asks the box1 portion only when box10 is positive. For a consistent zero box10 its portion is also zero, so both expressions return zero; for positive box10 the subtraction is identical. w2.box10_bad refuses a portion greater than box10 in the subtraction path. This is not an equivalence claim for unanswered or inconsistent stand-alone inputs; the project early exit avoids an unnecessary question.

Ruling: model error; the second sum omits W-2 code EE while including code H. Form8880 (2025) p.2 Line2 includes designated Roth contributions, and iw2w3 (2025) p.21 CodeEE identifies governmental 457(b) designated Roth contributions. CodeH is explicitly excluded by the project w2.code_h refusal, but codeEE is supported. With $1000 of codeEE and every other deferral zero, the project gives $1000 and the second zero. The evaluator witness is .transcription/w2-flash-ee-witness.json. The omitted early exits also differ on partial inputs; no blanket identity is claimed.

Ruling: scope/representation on completed consistent W-2 inputs; this maximum-reasoning response now includes all supported D/E/F/S/AA/BB/EE amounts. Positive codeH is excluded by project w2.code_h at sav_listed (its Schedule1 deduction is outside scope). For governmental G, w2.g_bad requires elective part E <= total G, so the model min(E,G) equals the project E; for non-governmental or absent G both contribute zero. box12_any=False means no listed amounts. f8880 (2025) p.2 Line2 and iw2w3 pp.20-21 establish the elective governmental G portion and designated Roth codes. An offline comparison of the actual model expression agrees across1152 admitted code/amount combinations (.transcription/w2-max-accepted-domain-proof.json). Refusal behavior and inconsistent/unanswered entries are not asserted equivalent.
